data.name: Moksha
data.gender_notes: Moksha is used as a unisex name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit root muc, 'to release' — mokṣa, 'liberation'. Its root is Sanskrit muc (मुच्). The ultimate goal in Hindu philosophy. Moksha is a Sanskrit name meaning “Liberation; release; emancipation”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Moksha expresses “Liberation; release; emancipation”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit root muc, 'to release' — mokṣa, 'liberation'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Moksha total 22, reducing to 4. Number 4 is associated with discipline, order and steady effort.

vedic_reference.note: Moksha is a term from Hinduism and Buddhism that refers to the ultimate goal of life, which is liberation from the cycle of birth and death through self-realization or enlightenment. In the Vedas and Upanishads, it is described as the final stage of human evolution and the ultimate bliss or peace.
